prize_parts.citation: for discoveries of the physiology and active molecular forms of glucagon-like peptide-1 that made possible incretin-based therapy of type 2 diabetes and obesity

statement.case_for: My preferred configuration is unchanged: a single-part B010 prize to Holst, Drucker and Mojsov. The case rests on the discovery chain and not on the fact that all six openings placed it first. Holst established GLP-1 secretion and its actions in humans, Mojsov identified the biologically active GLP-1(7-36) form, and Drucker characterised GLP-1 and GLP-2 biology, receptor pharmacology and the therapeutic rationale. The consequence is a mechanism confirmed independently over decades, large randomized outcome trials in diabetes and obesity, and growing cardiovascular and renal evidence. I see no maturity concern. Keeping the prize to one achievement is also the cleaner choice under the three-person ceiling: a second part would force one of the three GLP-1 credits to be cut, and I do not think any of them can be removed without damaging the citation.
statement.case_against: The costs remain real after round 1. Lotte Bjerre Knudsen's engineering of long-acting agonists is what turned the physiology into a medicine, and excluding her risks a prize that reads as incomplete. Mojsov's priority for the active peptide is contested against early peptide workers such as Habener, who are not among the credited names, and the supplied record does not let us settle that chronology; several of our round-1 statements, including mine, rest on recalled history. A physiology-anchored citation also invites the criticism that the pharmaceutical step was left unrecognised. I judge these costs acceptable for a prize about discovery, but they are costs and not settled matters.

responses.point: The chair opened with Holst, Drucker and Knudsen, and asked in the round-1 summary whether the citation must name the therapeutic invention, and what wording stops the Knudsen exclusion from reading as an oversight.
responses.response: I note and welcome that you moved to Holst, Drucker and Mojsov. On your question, I would keep the citation on the physiology and active molecular forms of GLP-1 and state the therapy as the consequence they made possible, as the current wording does. That reads as a principled boundary between discovery and development. It does not remove the cost, and I would not claim it does. Knudsen's work was a scientific contribution as well as an industrial one, and the citation should not describe it as merely industrial. If the committee decides the prize must name the invention of the long-acting agonists, I would then reconsider, but I would not do so by dropping Mojsov, because the active peptide is what defined what the drugs had to mimic.

responses.point: Sandberg keeps B004 (Mori and Walter) as the second choice for its clean attribution and conceptual originality, and notes that her attribution view on B010 rests on recalled history.
responses.response: I agree that the Mojsov and Habener question cannot be resolved from the supplied record, and I think we should say so openly and not let recalled history carry the decision. Where the record is silent, what I can rely on is that the identification of the active GLP-1(7-36) form is described as decisive by every member, including those who regard her credit as contested. On B004 as the fallback, I still rank it below B028. The mechanism is textbook and the Mori and Walter pairing is natural, but I weigh demonstrated medical consequence more heavily for this prize, and the Ron and integrated stress response boundary adds a citation problem. I would not treat clean attribution as strength of the case. I disclose my co-authorship with you again for transparency, and it does not affect this view.

responses.point: Wahren-Herlenius ranks CAR-T second and keeps Mojsov in the trio because contested credit argues for careful wording, not omission.
responses.response: I agree on keeping Mojsov and on careful wording. On CAR-T, I accept your view that it is a new modality with durable remissions in B-cell malignancies, and it is the alternative I would test first. My hesitation is the same as the one Perlmann and Sandberg raised: Eshhar's early chimeric receptor work is outside the credited names, Rosenberg's contribution is broader adoptive transfer, and the 2018 immunotherapy prize raises whether this is a distinct achievement. Until the committee defines what is being rewarded, whether receptor design, clinical translation or adoptive cell therapy, I would not move it above B010, where the discovery arc and clinical proof are both complete.

responses.point: Perlmann would accept a B010 citation that makes the physiology explicit, and calls B004 the best fallback if the GLP-1 credit cannot be settled, while cautioning against treating clean attribution as a stronger case.
responses.response: I agree with both points. The citation should lead with physiology and active molecular forms, and I accept that an attribution dispute alone is not a reason to switch to a prize that is cleaner but of less demonstrated medical impact. Where we differ slightly is the order of fallbacks. You would use B004 if the GLP-1 credit fails, whereas I would test B028 first because its clinical confirmation is stronger, with B004 a close second if the committee prefers a basic-science year. I also take your point that the question of which discovery changed the field applies equally to organoids, and I have not changed my view that B008 is a tool whose medical consequences are still prospective.

uncertainties: Whether the supplied record supports Mojsov's priority for the active peptide over Habener and other early contributors; I cannot establish this from the record and the committee should avoid deciding on recalled history.
Whether the committee will insist that the citation name the therapeutic invention, which would put Knudsen into the three and require dropping one of Holst, Drucker or Mojsov.
How the committee should define the CAR-T achievement after the 2018 immunotherapy prize, and whether Eshhar's omission is defensible.
Whether B004's lack of established therapeutic translation should count against it, and where the boundary with Ron and the integrated stress response would be drawn.
statement.conflict_note: No conflict involving a credited name on the shortlist. My documented co-authorship (spatial transcriptomics, Science 2016; eight works with Rickard Sandberg) concerns people and fields outside the shortlisted ballots, and I infer no further relationship from shared institutions. The round-1 disclosures of other members name no credited shortlist name, and nothing in round 1 changes my disclosure.
